Staff movements during the month were minimal, comprising the
departure and replacement of one gardener's labourer at Vaucluse House.
Mrs. O'Connor, whom Trustees will no doubt recall proceeded on leave in
February, has had the misfortune to break her arm and is still absent in
hospital at the time of writing. Exact details of her return are not yet
known, but Mrs.Gale will continue to relieve as required and I shall see that
the excellent Mrs. O'Connor receives her maximum holiday and sick leave
eligibility. Nielsen Park permanent staff remain as in previous months and
the peripatetic tendencies of unemployed relief workers continues - however,
we are getting some work out of them and as it is not costing us anything
(except perhaps a few extra overtime hours for me) - so be it. As we are
allowed $27.79 per man per week over and above wages for the purchase of tools
and equipment for them to use, this is a further compensation.

In conclusion, whilst on the one hand I regret that I am
not yet in a position to submit a detailed formal report upon the survey the
Trust has instructed me to carry out upon Nielsen Park operations, this is
not due to any dereliction of duty but rather to caution. All I would like to
say on this subject at this stage is that I find the whole situation an
incredibly complex one and its very complexity convinces me that there is a
need to proceed with extreme caution. Particularly is this so when, whatever
faults there may be, Nielsen Park at least continues to function in that it is
currently open daily for those who wish to use it and I must say that to do
anything drastic at this stage of the 1972/73 swimming season and thus perhaps
precipitate a crisis would be folly indeed. My own view is that the best (and
for that matter the fairest) plan, is for me to continue my present observations,
to continue the gradual "tightening up" process which is currently taking place
and for the whole matter to be reviewed during the Winter months in time to
